title: Enhanced schema error context and toggleable strict response mode (OpenAI compat)
author: Aisha Menon
description: Motivation: improve developer visibility when structured-output/JSON-schema validation fails while preserving streaming and OpenAI-compat semantics. This PR introduces a toggleable strict response mode and an enriched error envelope so clients (and the Console) can understand: whether a violation originated from the model, the client prompt, or the inference runtime; a machine-friendly error_code; a human summary; location pointers (byte/token offsets or JSON path); and an optional "closest valid example" hint. The implementation maintains backward compatibility: default is permissive (existing behavior unchanged) and strictness is opt-in via a new response_format.strict_response_mode boolean and response_format.schema.strictness setting. Runtime: lightweight validators are attached to streaming checkpoints so partial streams can be annotated and, on terminal violations, a grace-path is taken to emit an actionable rejection event without corrupting existing streams. Tool/function-calling: added fencing so tool calls are only emitted when the response passes a schema gate (configurable per-route) to avoid partial tool invocations from malformed outputs. Telemetry: schema-mismatch events are recorded with hashed context to aid evaluation while avoiding PII. API surface: OpenAI adapter accepts the new flags and maps behavior predictably; clients using OpenAI-compat will get equivalent fields via the options block. Docs/tests: added API docs, migration notes and 1:1 OpenAI-compat examples, plus unit/integration/e2e streaming replay tests. Rollout plan: feature gated, canary to 10% traffic, enable for internal customers first. Performance: microbenchmarks show median p50 latency impact <1.5% and throughput within 2% under typical batching. Checklist: [x] unit tests, [x] integration tests, [x] e2e streaming tests with replay, [x] docs updated, [x] telemetry hooks, [x] canary gating. Related: ENG-4023, PM-88, support case SUP-912.

release_notes: Add optional strict_response_mode and richer schema error envelopes for structured output. Default behavior unchanged; opt-in strict mode can be enabled per-request or per-route. Improves debugging and opens controlled strict validation for tool calls.
